Digital Marketing Foundations & Website Optimization 
In today’s digital-first world, having a strong online presence is essential for any brand’s success. Week 1 introduces you 
to the core principles of digital marketing and highlights the importance of website optimization as the foundation for all 
online marketing efforts. You will learn how a well-structured, user-friendly, and search-optimized website acts as the 
central hub for driving traffic, engaging users, and converting visitors into customers. 
In week 1, Digital Marketing Foundations & Website Optimization, we will learn 
● The evolution of digital marketing and current consumer trends. 
● The differences between digital and traditional marketing, and how to craft an effective digital marketing 
strategy. 
● Various digital marketing channels and how to leverage them. 
● The transformative role of AI in digital marketing, including predictive analytics, chatbots, and personalization.

AI in Digital and Social Media Marketing: An Introduction 
Artificial Intelligence (AI) is no longer a futuristic concept but a present-day reality that is significantly transforming digital 
marketing. It is revolutionizing how businesses connect with their audiences, deliver personalized experiences, and 
optimize marketing campaigns. AI-powered tools are capable of predicting consumer behavior and enabling chatbots to 
provide instant responses to customer queries. This allows brands to deliver the right message to the right audience at 
the right time effortlessly.

be time-consuming for humans. For instance, AI recommends products based on Browse history, optimizes ad campaigns

orders dosa on weekends, their AI system proactively triggers personalized ads or push notifications at the opportune 
moment. This is a prime example of AI-powered predictive marketing, where AI helps brands understand what customers

Evolution of Digital Marketing 
The digital marketing landscape has undergone a dramatic transformation, evolving from simple banner ads to 
sophisticated AI-driven predictive marketing. 
The 1990s: The Dawn of the Internet and Banner Ads 
The 1990s marked a pivotal shift with the advent of the internet. The first online ad was a simple banner that read, "Have 
you ever clicked your mouse right here? You will". This curiosity-driven ad successfully engaged early internet users. 
Businesses quickly recognized the potential of advertising online, leading to the birth of banner ads. A significant 
game-changer during this era was the launch of Google in 1998, which made s

game-changer during this era was the launch of Google in 1998, which made searching for information accessible and 
prompted marketers to understand the importance of search engine rankings. Being at the top of search results became 
crucial for businesses. 
Early 2000s: The Rise of Emails and SEO 
The early 2000s saw a surge in email marketing, with companies sending thousands of emails in hopes of driving sales. 
However, this led to user annoyance and the development of spam filters. Concurrently, Search Engine Optimization 
(SEO) became a dominant force. Businesses aimed to rank high on Google by stuffing keywords into their web pages, and 
some even resorted to "sneaky tricks" like using invisible keywords. Google, in response, continuously improved its 
algorithm to deliver more relevant search results.

Traditional Marketing vs. Digital Marketing 
Understanding the differences between traditional and digital marketing is crucial for crafting effective strategies. 
1. Audience Reach: Traditional marketing, such as TV or newspaper ads, casts a wide net, reaching a broad 
audience without much control over who sees the ad. Digital marketing, however, allows for precise targeting of 
specific demographics based on age, location, interests, or past buying behavior, ensuring marketing efforts are 
efficient. 
2. Cost: Traditional marketing can be very expensive, especially for large-scale campaigns like TV commercials 
during prime time. Digital marketing is generally more cost-effective, offering flexibility in spending and 
scalability, which allows small businesses to compete with larger companies.

scalability, which allows small businesses to compete with larger companies. 
3. Engagement: Traditional marketing is largely one-way communication, with limited direct interaction from the 
audience. Digital marketing, in contrast, is interactive, allowing consumers to comment, like, share, and ask 
questions directly on platforms like Instagram or Facebook. This fosters a deeper connection with the audience.

through tools like Google Analytics and Facebook Insights, enabling businesses to measure clicks, website dwell 
time, and purchases, allowing for precise adjustments.

SLIDE 2 — ABSTRACT
• Social platforms are widely used for sharing URLs, making them attractive targets for phishing and malware
distribution.
• Attackers use shortened, obfuscated, deceptive and newly generated URLs to evade conventional detection
systems.
• Traditional blacklist-based methods may fail to detect previously unseen malicious links.
• The proposed system analyzes URLs collected from social platforms using URL characteristics and
search-engine evidence.
• Machine-learning/deep-learning models classify links as Benign, Suspicious or Malicious.
• A risk score and explanation are generated to support automated warning and detection.

SLIDE 3 — INTRODUCTION
• Social media enables rapid propagation of URLs among large numbers of users.
• Malicious links may lead to phishing websites, malware downloads, fake login pages, scams and credential
theft.
• Attackers frequently modify URLs to bypass existing security mechanisms.
• URL-based ML/DL techniques can identify suspicious structural and semantic patterns.
• Search-engine analysis provides an additional contextual evidence layer for evaluating domains and URLs.
• This project combines social-platform data + URL analysis + search-engine evidence.
SLIDE 4 — PROBLEM STATEMENT
Existing malicious-link detection systems often rely on blacklists or URL-level features and may fail to identify
newly generated, obfuscated or rapidly changing malicious links shared through social platforms.
